title: Who Will Succeed Xi Jinping?
gist: Deng Yuwen reads the pre-Fifth Plenum provincial reshuffles as a generational shift (1964–69 cohort to party secretaryships, 1970s cohort to governorships) and argues Xi will likely rule to ~2037, building a pool of successors born 1967–1975 rather than naming an heir; his first criterion is protection of his legacy, so the 21st Party Congress in 2027 will show only who is in the final stretch.

insights.claim: Zhu Zhongming, born in 1972, was promoted on Sept. 4 from deputy party secretary of Shanghai to acting mayor, which many observers took as a sign he is being groomed as Xi Jinping's successor, though the author says matters are not so simple.
insights.speaker: Deng Yuwen
insights.so_what: Shanghai leadership is a classic springboard; track Zhu's rise as a succession indicator.

insights.claim: On Sept. 23 Anhui, Henan and Fujian got new party secretaries (Li Lecheng and Zhou Zuyi, both born 1965, and Zhao Long, born 1967), and on Oct. 24 Wang Zhijun took Hunan and Mo Gaoyi took Yunnan.
insights.speaker: Deng Yuwen
insights.so_what: Provincial leadership turnover shapes local policy priorities and the 2027 Central Committee lineup.
insights.locator: But matters are not so simple.

insights.claim: Chinese provincial party secretary posts are increasingly going to officials born 1964–1969 while governorships are opening to officials born in the 1970s, marking a clear generational shift.
insights.speaker: Deng Yuwen
insights.so_what: Generational turnover in the CCP signals the shape of China's 2030s leadership and policy continuity.
insights.quote: Provincial party secretary positions are increasingly going to officials born between 1964 and 1969, while governorships are opening up to officials born in the 1970s.
insights.locator: This reveals a clear generational shift.

insights.claim: Officials born around 1970 already at provincial/ministerial rank include Zhejiang Gov. Liu Jie, Jiangsu Gov. Liu Xiaotao, Guangxi's Wei Tao, Shanxi's Lu Dongliang (1973), Emergency Management Minister Zhang Chengzhong, SASAC chairman Cheng Fubo and Youth League chief A Dong.
insights.speaker: Deng Yuwen
insights.so_what: These names form the watchlist for Politburo promotions at the 21st Party Congress.

insights.claim: Officials born in the 1970s, recently labeled 'young cadres,' are now entering the core of senior Chinese officialdom en masse.
insights.speaker: Deng Yuwen
insights.so_what: A new cohort will run China's provinces and SOEs through the 2030s.
insights.quote: Now they are beginning to enter the real core of senior officialdom en masse.
insights.locator: Only a few years ago, officials

insights.claim: Deng Yuwen argues Xi's first criterion for a successor is protection of his political legacy, not mere personal loyalty or the strongest résumé.
insights.speaker: Deng Yuwen
insights.so_what: Implies strong policy continuity (Xi Thought, party-centric governance) beyond Xi's tenure; low odds of reformist pivot.
insights.quote: the first criterion is the protection of his political legacy
insights.locator: Both matter, but for a leader

insights.claim: Xi wants to avoid a successor who, like Khrushchev with Stalin, denounces him after death, or who, like Deng Xiaoping after Mao, preserves his status while changing the system.
insights.speaker: Deng Yuwen
insights.so_what: Successor selection is biased toward continuity of ideology and system.
insights.locator: A successor must be politically reliable

insights.claim: Because Xi himself was mild as heir and only centralized power after taking office, he knows obedience today does not guarantee predictability once a successor holds supreme power, creating a dilemma between capability and controllability.
insights.speaker: Deng Yuwen
insights.so_what: The capability-vs-controllability tradeoff raises the risk of a weaker or delayed transition.
insights.quote: Supreme power changes political behavior. Xi understands this better than most.
insights.locator: An official who obeys Xi today

insights.claim: China's 2030s leader will face US technological and geopolitical competition, possible Taiwan military risks, and a party-state with more than 100 million CCP members and a vast state-owned economy.
insights.speaker: Deng Yuwen
insights.so_what: Frames the long-run risk set (Taiwan, US rivalry, SOEs) any successor inherits.
insights.locator: The third criterion is the ability to govern.

insights.claim: Running Beijing, Shanghai, Guangdong, Jiangsu and Zhejiang serves as a crisis-performance test for successor candidates, since handling downturns, accidents, unrest or foreign confrontation matters more than routine work.
insights.speaker: Deng Yuwen
insights.so_what: Watch who gets top posts in these provinces as succession signals.
insights.locator: This is why Beijing, Shanghai, Guangdong

insights.claim: Deng Yuwen has long argued Xi Jinping is likely to remain in power for two more terms, roughly 2027 to 2037, so he has no need to name a successor now.
insights.speaker: Deng Yuwen
insights.so_what: Base case of Xi rule to 2037 implies a decade of policy continuity in China.
insights.quote: I have argued that Xi is likely to remain in power for another two terms, roughly from 2027 to 2037.
insights.locator: For several years, I have argued

insights.claim: Naming an heir early would create a second center of power that officials gravitate toward, which is unattractive to a leader emphasizing centralized control, so Xi is more likely to build a pool of possible successors.
insights.speaker: Deng Yuwen
insights.so_what: Expect no clear heir — succession uncertainty remains a tail risk for China.

insights.claim: Officials born between 1967 and 1975 are the most realistic successor pool; they would be 65–70 at a ~2037 handover, older than Xi or Hu Jintao at takeover, which could help ensure legacy fidelity.
insights.speaker: Deng Yuwen
insights.so_what: An older successor favors continuity over policy change.
insights.locator: Xi is therefore more likely at this stage

insights.claim: The author expects the 21st Central Committee's age center to shift to those born 1964–1974, with 1950s-born officials largely disappearing except for Xi and a few top leaders.
insights.speaker: Deng Yuwen
insights.so_what: Measurable test of the generational thesis at the 2027 congress.
insights.locator: I expect the age center of gravity

insights.claim: If post-1970 officials such as Zhu Zhongming, Lu Dongliang, Liu Jie or Liu Xiaotao enter the Politburo at the 21st Party Congress, that would be a strong succession signal; 1967–69-born figures like Zhao Long, Yin Yong and Zhao Gang are also in the pool.
insights.speaker: Deng Yuwen
insights.so_what: Concrete watchlist for the late-2027 congress.
insights.locator: If figures such as Zhao, Beijing Mayor

insights.claim: Deng Yuwen does not expect the 21st Party Congress to reveal Xi's successor, only who is in the final stretch of the race.
insights.speaker: Deng Yuwen
insights.so_what: Don't price a clean succession signal from the 2027 congress.
insights.quote: All it may tell us is who is in the final stretch of the race.
